title: The Tide of Junebug Creek
premise: Jude Coldharbour, a wedding planner who stopped believing in marriage after her own ended in a courthouse betrayal, is drafted into a small-town anonymous pen-pal program meant to heal feuds in Junebug Creek. Instead of pairing strangers, the town clerk's clerical error pairs Jude with Eli Marchetti, the county sheriff who once arrested her brother on a charge that never stuck — and whose letters, unsigned and unguarded, slowly become the only honest thing in her life. As they fall for each other on paper while warring in person over the fate of the creek lands her family has fished for generations, Jude must decide whether justice pursued outside the law is worth losing the one man who sees her whole. When the true culprit behind the land grab is exposed at the creek itself, Eli chooses conscience over badge, and Jude chooses to risk the whole heart instead of lending pieces.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent a decade listening to other people's love stories end badly. She now writes from a houseboat on an unnamed tributary, where she insists the water keeps better secrets than any witness stand.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She orchestrates a flawless wedding for a couple she privately pities, reciting her creed that the heart is trainable muscle. A letter arrives: Junebug Creek's reconciliation pen-pal program has assigned her a partner. Beat: armored competence cracking into unease.

chapters.title: Clerical Error
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The town clerk misfiles the pairings; Eli discovers his anonymous correspondent is Jude Coldharbour — the sister of the man he arrested, the woman who glares at him across every council meeting. He almost withdraws, then doesn't. Beat: guilty curiosity winning over duty.

chapters.title: First Ink
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Both write guarded opening letters, each certain they're deceiving a stranger. Jude vents about weddings; Eli confesses he no longer trusts his own instincts on the job. They recognize nothing yet. Beat: accidental intimacy under false names.

chapters.title: The Creek Runs Through It
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Back home, she learns a development consortium is buying out families along Junebug Creek — including hers — with suspiciously fast paperwork. Her brother Denny urges fighting dirty. Beat: the private feud becomes a public cause.

chapters.title: Sheriff's Burden
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Ordered to serve eviction notices along the creek, Eli stalls, sensing the deeds are wrong but finding no legal flaw. His letters to his pen pal grow more desperate and honest. Beat: duty beginning to chafe against conscience.

chapters.title: Enemies at the Grange Hall
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At a raucous town meeting, Jude and Eli clash publicly over the evictions, trading barbs that cut deeper than either expects. That night she writes her pen pal about 'a man I could hate if he weren't so tired.' Beat: enemies sharpening into mirrors.

chapters.title: What the Letters Know
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Rereading his correspondence, Eli realizes his pen pal understands him better than anyone alive — and suspects, with dread, who she might be. He writes one more letter anyway. Beat: the pull of honesty over self-protection.

chapters.title: Rain on the Deeds
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Digging through county records in a storm, Jude finds forged signatures linking the land purchases to Councilman Harrow Voss. She photographs everything, unsure whether to take it to the law or around it. Beat: justice becoming a personal project.

chapters.title: The Arrested Brother
chapters.summary: Denny's POV (interlude). Denny reflects on the arrest that broke his family, admitting he was carrying something that night — not what Eli thought, but enough to make him lie. Beat: complicating the enemy, seeding doubt about old verdicts.

chapters.title: Midsummer Confession
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the creek's midsummer festival, Jude and Eli are thrown together by a stranded canoe and a sudden storm. Sheltering in a boathouse, they talk for hours without armor — still not knowing they've already confessed more on paper. Beat: the heart forgetting its training.

chapters.title: Signed, Anonymous
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A phrase in her pen pal's latest letter — 'the boathouse rain' — stops her cold. She tests him with a detail only Eli would know, and his reply confirms it. Beat: revelation as vertigo; fury and longing colliding.

chapters.title: Burn Letter
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Realizing Jude knows, Eli writes a full confession of the arrest, his doubts, and his feelings — then hesitates over the send. Denny confronts him at the station, forcing the truth into the open between all three. Beat: the cost of concealment coming due.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude reads Eli's confession letter and recognizes her own creed failing: the heart isn't containable after all. But before she can answer, Voss's men ransack her office and steal her evidence file. Beat: love declared just as danger arrives.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With the evidence gone and the sheriff's department quietly compromised, Jude proposes going around the law entirely: recover Voss's original ledger from the county annex. Eli must choose his badge or her plan. Beat: alliance forged where duty ends.

chapters.title: Harrow Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV (villain interlude). Voss, charming and ruthless, reveals he engineered the pen-pal pairings deliberately — to keep the Coldharbours and their sheriff distracted while the final deed closes Friday. Beat: the stakes tighten; the romance was weaponized.

chapters.title: The Longest Week
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Planning the annex retrieval like her best wedding — timelines, contingencies, guest lists of allies — Jude rebuilds trust with Eli in stolen hours. They finally speak the letters aloud to each other. Beat: love against the clock.

chapters.title: Night at the Annex
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The retrieval goes wrong; a silent alarm brings Voss's fixers, and Eli takes a beating shielding Jude and the ledger. They escape with proof but leave blood and fingerprints behind. Beat: climax rising — sacrifice made real.

chapters.title: Badge on the Table
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Rather than let Voss bury the ledger, Eli walks into the council meeting, resigns his badge in front of the town, and reads the ledger aloud. Chaos erupts; Voss moves to have them both arrested. Beat: the climax — conscience over career.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The town, moved by years of quiet grievances, stands up one by one — Denny first, testifying to what really happened the night of his arrest. Voss's forgery unravels publicly. Beat: justice outside the law vindicated by community.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the aftermath, Eli faces an internal review and an uncertain future; Jude faces the scarier thing — permanence. At the creek bank where it began, they exchange final letters, signed this time with their names. Beat: tenderness after the storm.

chapters.title: A Wedding, After All
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Months later, Jude plans one last wedding — her own, small and imperfect, on the repaired banks of Junebug Creek, with Denny as witness and the town as congregation. She retires her muscle theory out loud. Beat: resolution; belief rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Tide of Junebug Creek
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year on: the creek protected, Eli teaching a new generation of deputies about conscience, Jude writing letters to strangers who need honest words. The last image is two unsent drafts in a drawer, kept like promises already kept. Beat: peace earned, love ongoing.
